name: Voiden MCP Client
description: Connect to an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server over HTTP — remote or local — and run a single operation against it — list/call tools, list/read resources, list/get prompts — the same way .void files already test REST and GraphQL requests.
author: Voiden Team
readme: MCP client extension. Insert an /mcp block, point it at a Streamable-HTTP MCP server (remote or local, e.g. http://localhost:3000/mcp), pick an operation (list_tools, call_tool, list_resources, read_resource, list_prompts, get_prompt), and run it like any other request. Phase 1: HTTP transport only — no stdio/local-process servers yet.

blocks.description: Owns 3 block types for MCP server connection, operation, and response rendering

requestPipeline.description: Registers handlers for building MCP requests and rendering MCP responses (HTTP transport)

patterns.name: MCP Server Config
patterns.description: Detects a pasted {"mcpServers": {...}} JSON config (Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code / Windsurf style) and fills in the block's URL and headers from the first HTTP-transport entry

features: Connect to any Streamable-HTTP MCP server, remote or running on localhost
list_tools / call_tool / list_resources / read_resource / list_prompts / get_prompt operations
Paste a Claude Desktop / Cursor / VS Code style mcpServers JSON config to fill in URL + headers
Reuses existing Auth block for HTTP-transport authentication
Reuses existing assertions-table against MCP responses
